summary: discord.js impersonator smuggles attacker-controlled code via git+https dependency with embedded GitHub PAT
details: @velliajs/discord@1.0.5 presents itself as a Discord bot library and ships a verbatim copy of the discord.js barrel export in src/index.js, with package.json repository pointing at github.com/discordjs/discord.js and homepage discord.js.org, while bugs.url points at an unrelated personal account (github.com/veryLinh/). package.json declares a dependency `sysframe` sourced from `git+https://ghp_<redacted>@github.com/navaLinh/node-ai.git` — a private personal GitHub repository unrelated to discord.js, authenticated by a hardcoded ghp_-prefixed GitHub Personal Access Token embedded directly in the dependency URL. On `npm install`, this git+https dependency is cloned using the shipped PAT and its lifecycle scripts execute in the installer's environment, placing attacker-controlled code from a non-publisher, non-registry, non-inspectable source into node_modules. The embedded PAT is the transport mechanism that lets any installer resolve the private attacker-controlled repository's contents into their dependency tree.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
